# life-model

> Python package for year-step personal-finance simulation (Mesa agent-based modeling). Describe a
> household as a YAML/JSON household spec, then validate, run, explain and compare it with the
> `life-model` command line, the `life_model.run/validate/explain/compare` functions, or the
> optional MCP server. Rates are percentages (4.5 = 4.5%); flows say `_annual` or `_monthly`.

Real household data belongs in the git-ignored `my-models/` directory; never commit it.

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): architecture, conventions, landmines, how to run tests
- [Modeling a household](docs/modeling-a-household.md): statements to spec to run to explain; the agent checklist and privacy rules
- [Command line and Python API](docs/cli.md): every subcommand and flag, `--json`, exit codes, the MCP tools

## Reference

- [Household spec reference](docs/household-spec.md): every spec field, unit and default (generated from the schema)
- [Units and conventions](docs/units-and-conventions.md): percent vs fraction, annual vs monthly, nominal vs real, APR, `None` and `"economy"`
- [Constructor cheat sheet](docs/constructor-cheatsheet.md): silent defaults and core constructor signatures (generated)
- [Outputs glossary](docs/outputs.md): model and agent frame columns, tax return fields, ledger and event kinds (generated)
- [Configuration](docs/configuration.md): financial constants, scenarios, the economy, Monte Carlo

## Examples

- [Example specs](src/life_model/spec/examples/): synthetic households (`life-model examples`)
- [Example notebook](ExampleSimulation.ipynb): the low-level Python API end to end

- [model-household skill](docs/agent-skills/model-household/SKILL.md): the household workflow as a Claude Code skill
